newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Tokyo and Hong Kong up slightly, Bombay hit hard.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo and Hong Kong up slightly, Bombay hit hard.

text.p: Tokyo and Hong Kong shares posted modest gains on Friday but several other Asian bourses moved more dramatically.
Thailand, Taiwan, Jakarta and Kuala Lumpur added more than one percent but Seoul and Bombay were heavy losers, the Indian market down 2.50 percent on disappointing company results.
Brokers said Tokyo trading was cautious and mostly directionless ahead of next Wednesday's Bank of Japan "tankan" survey of business sentiment.

The key Nikkei 225 average was up 72.77 points or 0.34 percent to finish at 21,216.11, its highest level for the day. Aggressive investor buying, which lifted the Nikkei average earlier this week, withered and brokers expect range-bound trade next week, brokers said.
"Sentiment seems to have made a turn for the better, but the index remains in a boxed range," said Kaoru Ichikawa, a senior trader at Kokusai Securities Co Ltd.
A strategist at Nomura Securities Co Ltd, Masaaki Higashida, said: "We probably won't see further buying from institutional investors next week as the end of the month is approaching."
After retreating from a record-setting rally on Thursday, Hong Kong stocks added 0.13 percent, buoyed by property investment counters.
The mood was boosted after a major commercial and office building sold for a high price in the territory, but profit-taking in other areas limited gains.
The key Hang Seng index rose 17.23 points to 13,116.79.
Thai stocks rallied strongly as retail speculators bet on successful talks among partners of coalition leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh in sharing cabinet portfolios, analysts said.
The SET Index closed 14.95 points up, or 1.56 percent, to 970.30.
"I think retail buying was boosted by expectations that the market would rebound," said Kanjanee Kangwanpornsiri, assistant Managing Director at Thai Fuji.

Taiwan share prices added 1.03 percent to a 22-month high close as a recent bull run revived on active buying in the heavily weighted financial sector and fundamentals-backed electronic shares, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 68.90 points higher at 6,761.39, its highest finish since January 11, 1995.
Jakarta share prices ended 1.64 percent up ahead of the listing of giant Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) on the back of bargain-hunting and fresh buying in some big-caps, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 9.87 points, or 1.64 percent to close at 612.86 points after hitting an intra-day high of 614.52 points in late trading.
"The market is likely to be more active in the coming week, enlivened by the listing of BNI," said Motoo Murata, resident senior economist of the Daiwa Institute of Research.
Bombay shares slid 2.49 percent as funds and punters sold on disappointing first-half earnings announcements and gloomy industrial growth data, traders said.
Bombay's benchmark stocks index dropped 75.83 points to a provisional close of 2967.47.
Seoul stocks ended sharply lower as the already fragile market sentiment was affected by a government plan to sell Korea Telecom shares, brokers said.
A bribery scandal involving the president of a leading commercial bank also affected the overall mood, they said.
The composite index was down 1.81 percent, or 13.45 points to a provisional close of 731.44.
"It's hard to blame any one specific factor for today's fall, but a longstanding mix of factors and the lack of good news were to blame," said Kim Heung-shik of Hyundai Securities.
The state Korean Broadcasting System reported that the president of SEOULBANK was under investigation on charges of taking kickbacks from companies in return for loans.
At 11.13 GMT, the dollar traded at 111.32/1.37 yen and 1.5013/18 marks.
Hong Kong gold prices were slightly higher to end at $376.65/377.15 an ounce against Thursday's New York close of $376.30/80.
SIMEX Brent crude futures continued to climb, the prompt January contract last trading at $23.31 per barrel, up 18 cents from London's close.
